To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the change blindness effect occurs only after a brief blank screen, not after a brief scene that does not change, and that the change blindness is reduced when the blank screen is replaced with a blank screen that is followed by a scene that is the same as the first scene.
the failure to detect changes across brief interruptions depends on initial preview and that the nature of the interruption is important.

(a) change blindness is induced by brief blank intervals between scenes, (b) change blindness is reduced by a brief preview of the first scene, (c) change blindness is not reduced when the preview is followed by a brief blank interval, (d) change blindness is increased by longer blank intervals between scenes (e) change blindness is also increased by longer blank interruptions in the course of a scene, and (f) change blindness is greater for changes to objects than to background
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How does attentional focus influence visual perception?
understanding the mechanisms of visual change detection.
the question: How do we perceive change in the world?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
change blindness is a consequence of the fact that attention is needed for the maintenance of information in visual short-term memory.
“the failure of observers to detect changes across brief interruptions is caused by the volatility of representations at early stages of processing”.
change blindness is caused by the failure of attention to reorient from the interruption to the target of change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the visual system is not designed for change detection, but for the recognition of familiar objects and scenes.
we have found that change blindness is a failure of perception, not a failure of memory.
change blindness occurs because the early stages of processing are inherently volatile and that attention is required to stabilize them sufficiently for change detection to occur.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to pay more attention to the role of attention in perception.
we should not take the fact that we can see something for granted. The ability to perceive
